blocks.text:
From the Argentine capital, you will take a day trip across the Río de la Plata to Montevideo. You will then visit Iguazu Falls from both the Argentine and Brazilian sides. The final part of the journey is in Brazil: Rio de Janeiro, Corcovado, Sugar Loaf and time on the coast in Búzios.

This itinerary brings together major cities, national parks, glaciers, waterfalls, the ocean and several South American cultures. Chile introduces you to mountain scenery and wine country, Argentina to Patagonia, tango and gastronomy, Uruguay to Montevideo's colonial architecture, and Brazil to the tropics, beaches and Rio's panoramic views.

## 4 countries in one journey

**Chile.** Your journey begins in a country of high mountains, well-known vineyards and strong natural contrasts. After Santiago, you will head far south to Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine, where lakes, fjords, waterfalls and pointed peaks replace the cityscape.

**Argentina.** Here, the programme combines Patagonia with a major city. In El Calafate, Perito Moreno is the main attraction; in Buenos Aires, you will explore historic neighbourhoods, enjoy tango and Argentine cuisine, and spend a day at an estancia for a Fiesta Gaucha.

**Uruguay.** A day trip to Montevideo adds another capital to your itinerary. The ferry across the Río de la Plata, Independence Square, Palacio Salvo, the old market and free time let you explore at an easy pace.

**Brazil.** First, you will see Iguazu from both sides of the border, then fly to Rio de Janeiro. After Corcovado, Sugar Loaf and the historic centre, your last days will be by the ocean in Búzios.
